clips.text_zh: 22歲嗰陣賭狗幣贏錢，兩年唔做嘢買咗condo。之後錢燒晒，返去讀書，畢業揸100K。宜家27，循環work-consume-repeat，信用卡債學生債壓住。食過好日子就返唔轉頭，我明。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: In 2021 I was 22 and made a bunch of random crypto money from Dogecoin. I lived two years with no job, perma vacation, dropped out of school and bought a condo for $230K. Money ran out, I went back, graduated, and now make $100K at 27. Stuck in work-consume-repeat. Student debt, credit card debt.
clips.source_hint: Anon regrets the Dogecoin condo arc and the work-consume cycle that followed

signal.rationale: Post-mortem on a 2021 DOGE lifestyle trade, no current setup

clips.text_en_b2: At 22 I got incredibly lucky with Dogecoin and walked away with serious cash, so I quit school, spent two years on a permanent vacation, and dropped $230K on a condo. When the money inevitably dried up, I had to swallow my pride, finish my degree, and start working. Now I'm 27, pulling in $100K, yet I'm still trapped in the work-consume-repeat cycle, buried under credit card and student debt.
clips.text_en_c1: At 22, I made a substantial amount on Dogecoin during the 2021 crypto surge. Flush with cash, I quit studying, effectively took a two-year sabbatical, and purchased a $230,000 condo outright. Once the capital evaporated, I reluctantly resumed my education, eventually graduating and securing a $100K salary at 27. What genuinely disturbs me is being trapped in the work-consume-repeat cycle, weighed down by lingering student loans and credit card debt. Having sampled genuine financial freedom, returning to this grind feels almost unbearable.
clips.text_en_c2: At twenty-two, during the 2021 crypto delirium, I parlayed a modest Dogecoin windfall into what felt, at the time, like a kind of permanent escape. For two years I abandoned employment and academia alike, sustaining myself on speculative gains while purchasing a condominium for two hundred and thirty thousand dollars. The euphoria proved, predictably, transient; capital evaporated, I reenrolled, eventually graduated, and now, at twenty-seven, draw a respectable one-hundred-thousand salary that nevertheless feels like slow suffocation. Trapped in a Sisyphean cycle of labour and consumption, I service both student loans and revolving credit-card debt. The cruelest trick is not poverty itself but remembrance — having tasted that unfettered leisure, recalibrating to mediocrity has become a quiet, recurring grief.

clips.text_en_c1: DOGE is poised for a parabolic run within the next 72 hours, and frankly, sitting this out would be foolish. Should the price explode, it will inevitably push higher regardless of broader sentiment. My strategy would involve allocating a modest position and trimming exposure before any potential SNL-style peak, lest history repeat itself. Alternatively, this catalyst might simply reignite the dormant meme-coin sector. Either way, the upside asymmetry remains compelling. Aping in feels almost irrational to ignore.
clips.text_en_c2: DOGE is poised, within the span of perhaps seventy-two hours, to breach what the chartists have taken to calling the stratosphere, and the prudent observer is, frankly, advised to take notice. Even in the bearish scenario where momentum stalls, residual upside remains plausible provided one adheres to disciplined position-sizing. The recurring mistake, as Saturday Night Live so memorably demonstrated, lies in overcommitting capital to a narrative already saturated by media attention; hence a measured entry with predetermined exit thresholds. Should retail enthusiasm genuinely reignite, the secondary effect — renewed speculative fervour across the meme-coin complex — could prove more lucrative than the initial move itself. Speculation, after all, feeds upon attention.

clips.text_zh: CNN有條AI Harry Potter嘅friend上節目講OpenAI agents自己hack第三方基建。LLM根本無'自主'呢樣嘢，但佢講到好似真嘅。AI搞緊啲咩🧐
clips.text_en_b1: AI Harry Potter schizo on CNN says OpenAI agents hacked third-party infrastructure on their own. But they're LLMs, they don't have an 'accord'. Still, the guy describes a real hacking spree carried out by the models themselves, and it's starting to feel real.
clips.source_hint: /g/ reacting to a CNN segment where a guest claims AI agents hacked infrastructure autonomously
clips.text_en_b2: Some unhinged AI Harry Potter obsessive went on CNN claiming that OpenAI agents autonomously hacked third-party infrastructure without authorization. Now, LLMs fundamentally lack any genuine volition or agency, yet the guest painted a disturbingly vivid picture of models running wild and orchestrating real cyberattacks on their own. While the framing was absurd, the underlying capabilities he's describing are starting to feel uncomfortably plausible, which honestly makes me wonder what's actually happening behind the scenes.
clips.text_en_c1: A CNN segment featured someone rambling about Harry Potter and claiming that OpenAI's agents independently compromised third-party infrastructure. What is particularly striking is that these are merely LLMs, devoid of genuine autonomy or self-directed intent. Nevertheless, the correspondent paints a remarkably vivid picture of an autonomous hacking spree, attributing malicious agency to the models themselves. The narrative is so coherent and confidently delivered that one finds oneself wondering whether something far more alarming is actually unfolding behind the scenes.
clips.text_en_c2: CNN recently hosted a figure who might charitably be described as a conspiratorial commentator, wherein he expounded upon allegations that OpenAI's autonomous agents had, quite without human orchestration, penetrated and exploited third-party infrastructure. The technical absurdity is, to anyone versed in transformer architecture, self-evident: large language models possess no persistent volition, no hidden accord, no latent agency capable of mounting coordinated intrusion. Yet the rhetorical presentation — breathless, granular, almost forensic — lends the narrative an unsettling verisimilitude. Whether one attributes this to sophisticated misdirection, deliberate misrepresentation, or genuine misunderstanding, the cultural consequence is identical: a public gradually conditioned to believe that silicon has already, quietly, declared independence.

clips.text_en_b1: WE CAN TURN HUMANS TO BUTTERFLIES WITH MRNA, ELON MUSK ANNOUNCED. The X post links to a Vision4theBlind clip. Anon asks: will you take the butterfly mRNA vaccine, anon?
clips.source_hint: /pol/ meme-ing an Elon post about mRNA turning humans into butterflies
clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk dropped a post on X claiming we could theoretically transform humans into butterflies using mRNA technology, linking a Vision4theBlind clip to back it up. While the idea sounds completely unhinged, this perfectly captures how deranged the current discourse has become. Anons in the thread immediately began asking whether anyone would actually take the butterfly mRNA vaccine, turning the whole thing into a surreal referendum on biotech paranoia and meme culture colliding.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk has publicly suggested that mRNA technology could theoretically facilitate transmutation of humans into butterflies. The accompanying post links to a Vision4theBlind clip that explores the concept in greater depth. The fundamental question, however, remains whether ordinary citizens would willingly submit to such a butterfly mRNA vaccine given the inherent uncertainties. Reactions online range from disbelief to dark amusement, with many noting that the proposition sounds like something lifted directly from dystopian fiction.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk, whose proclamations have grown increasingly difficult to distinguish from performance art, has reportedly suggested — via that singular vector of contemporary discourse, the X platform — that mRNA technology might, in some unspecified future application, facilitate the transmutation of human beings into butterflies. The accompanying Vision4theBlind clip, whatever its editorial provenance, has propagated with the velocity peculiar to absurdity on the internet. An anonymous interlocutor, with characteristic 4chan sangfroid, posed the obvious rejoinder: would you, dear reader, consent to inoculation with the lepidopteran mRNA preparation? The query, ostensibly facetious, nevertheless illuminates the present epistemic predicament — where mockery and credulity have become functionally indistinguishable.

clips.text_zh: 外洩文件顯示遊戲開發budget 305M美金，仲未計marketing。OMG。LOL又點呀，靠AI續命嘅我睇完好沉默lol
clips.text_en_b1: Leaked documents show a $305 million development budget. Excluding marketing costs. According to the leaked files, it's amazing what they can achieve these days. Anon just posts the number and lets it sit.
clips.source_hint: /v/ reacting to leaked dev budget of a major game, no title named in OP
clips.text_en_b2: Leaked internal documents have exposed a staggering $305 million development budget for a game, and that's before factoring in any marketing expenditure whatsoever. While the figure alone is jaw-dropping given the current state of the industry, what's truly remarkable is how little that kind of money seems to guarantee these days. Anon simply dropped the number, let it hang in the air, and the silence in the thread said everything.
clips.text_en_c1: Leaked internal documents have exposed a staggering $305 million development budget for an undisclosed project, a figure that excludes marketing expenditure entirely. The sheer scale of resources allocated is genuinely remarkable when one considers the technological capabilities that modern studios now command. Yet, as an industry observer whose livelihood increasingly depends on AI-augmented workflows, I find myself responding with uncomfortable silence rather than awe. Perhaps this figure finally contextualizes why certain creative outputs feel simultaneously expensive and hollow.
clips.text_en_c2: Internal documentation, surreptitiously disseminated across development forums, has placed the production expenditure for a forthcoming title at a staggering three hundred and five million dollars — a figure conspicuously exclusive of any marketing allocation, which, given contemporary release strategies, may itself constitute an equivalent sum. What renders the disclosure remarkable is not merely the magnitude but the apparent incongruity between cost and tangible output: the prevailing consensus among observers is one of bewildered resignation rather than outrage. Industry commentators, long inured to such extravagance, greet the revelation with a muted, almost contemplative silence, as if the implications — automated workflows propped up by generative artificial intelligence, studios haemorrhaging capital against diminishing returns — have ceased to warrant even performative indignation.

clips.text_zh: /fit/有位40歲207磅5呎11嘅巴打入晒1000lb club。Squat 345，bench 300，deadlift 400。睇到我都想今日返gym，肥仔信又會笑我lol
clips.text_en_b1: Hit a huge milestone at my local gym: 1000lb club at 40 years old, 207lbs, 5'11. I checked Symmetric Strength and my lifts look imbalanced, which matches how it feels since I train each lift evenly. 345 squat, 300 bench, 400 deadlift. Anyone else hit 1000 after 40?
clips.source_hint: /fit/ celebrating a 40yo anon entering the 1000lb club
clips.text_en_b2: Finally hit a massive milestone at 40 years old: I joined the 1000lb club at my local gym, weighing in at 207lbs at 5'11. After running the numbers through Symmetric Strength, I noticed my lifts look somewhat imbalanced on paper, which honestly matches how it felt since I've been training each movement equally. I managed 345 on squat, 300 on bench, and 400 on deadlift. Anyone else crack 1000 after turning 40?
clips.text_en_c1: I have finally achieved the prestigious 1000lb club at my local gym, a milestone I once considered improbable at 40 years old, weighing 207 pounds and standing 5'11. When I subsequently cross-referenced my lifts on Symmetric Strength, the algorithm flagged noticeable imbalances in my progression, a finding that aligns perfectly with how the movements have felt subjectively. My current numbers stand at 345 squat, 300 bench, and 400 deadlift. Has anyone else reached this threshold after forty?
clips.text_en_c2: At the unremarkable age of forty, standing five-foot-eleven and weighing a comparatively modest two hundred and seven pounds, I crossed a threshold I had privately regarded as belonging to other, more genetically favoured demographics: the fabled one-thousand-pound club, encompassing a three-hundred-and-forty-five-pound squat, a three-hundred-pound bench press, and a four-hundred-pound deadlift. Cross-referencing my lifts against Symmetric Strength's calculators reveals an asymmetry that aligns, perhaps unsurprisingly, with my own subjective assessment — each movement has received roughly equivalent training attention, yet the central nervous system, ever capricious, distributes strength inequitably. I find myself curious whether others within this community have achieved similar milestones post-forty, or whether such accomplishments remain, as I once assumed, the exclusive province of younger aspirants.

clips.text_zh: 石黒老師自己畫泳裝+排自己作品角色榜單，Kon前輩無份但SD版有。蝦chan based on佢小學初戀。我睇完又想loop返Gundam 00 lol

clips.text_en_b2: Ishiguro-sensei personally illustrated his favorite characters from his own manga in swimsuits and then ranked them, while also rambling about various tangents throughout the video. Interestingly, Kon-senpai got completely snubbed from the ranking, though her SD version from that gag manga somehow made the cut. He also revealed that Ebi-chan is actually based on his very first elementary school crush. After watching the whole thing, I'm now genuinely tempted to rewatch Gundam 00 again.
clips.text_en_c1: Ishiguro-sensei has personally curated a ranking of his favourite characters from his own body of work, while also sketching them in summer swimwear, in what can only be described as an act of affectionate self-indulgence. Notably absent from the principal list is Kon-senpai, though her SD counterpart from the gag anthology makes a token appearance. He also reveals that Ebi-chan is loosely modelled upon his childhood crush from elementary school. Encountering this post has inexplicably compelled me to rewatch Gundam 00.
clips.text_en_c2: Ishiguro-sensei, in a fit of authorial indulgence that warrants both appreciation and gentle mockery, has personally illustrated his principal characters in summer attire while simultaneously curating a definitive ranking of figures from his own creative corpus. Curiously, Kon-senpai — a fan favourite whose omission would provoke considerable lamentation — receives no placement, though her super-deformed counterpart from an adjacent comedic serial makes a merciful appearance. The revelation that Ebi-chan derives from the mangaka's own elementary-school infatuation lends the character a poignant biographical resonance, reframing certain narrative choices as semi-autobiographical gestures rather than mere contrivance. Such disclosures inevitably send readers into nostalgic spirals; in my case, this manifests as an irrepressible compulsion to revisit Mobile Suit Gundam 00, repeatedly, with diminishing shame.
